policy_evidence.claim: The official Search API provides anonymous system access to published procurement notices for analysis and reuse, including use by commercial organisations.
policy_evidence.captured_excerpt: Published notices are anonymously accessible for analysis and reuse by systems, researchers, developers, and commercial organisations.

policy_evidence.claim: The TED legal notice permits commercial and non-commercial reuse of published procurement notices unless otherwise stated and dedicates SIMAP metadata to CC0.
policy_evidence.captured_excerpt: Published procurement notices may be freely reused commercially or non-commercially; SIMAP metadata is dedicated to the public domain under CC0.

policy_evidence.claim: The TED legal notice warns that identifiable private individuals and third-party works can require additional rights, so contact fields are excluded from collection.
policy_evidence.captured_excerpt: Identifiable private individuals and third-party works may require additional rights, so direct contact fields are outside this source contract.

policy_evidence.claim: The official eForms schema defines stable notice, procedure, organisation, and buyer-reference identifiers that can support provenance and independence checks.
policy_evidence.captured_excerpt: The schema defines notice, procedure, organisation, and buyer-reference identifiers for published procurement data.

policy_evidence.claim: The product requires a 90-day evidence window, stable independent-author checks, immutable provenance, and reviewable derived outputs.
policy_evidence.captured_excerpt: The product requires a 90-day window, stable independence checks, immutable provenance, and reviewable derived outputs.

data_classes.name: notice_title_and_description
data_classes.refresh_method: Refetch the published notice through the anonymous Search API.
data_classes.deletion_method: Delete normalized text and dependent derived outputs from local storage.

data_classes.name: notice_identifier
data_classes.refresh_method: Refetch by the published notice identifier.
data_classes.deletion_method: Delete the notice identifier with the local source record.

data_classes.name: procedure_identifier
data_classes.refresh_method: Refetch notices associated with the procedure identifier.
data_classes.deletion_method: Delete the procedure identifier with the local source record.

data_classes.name: canonical_notice_url
data_classes.refresh_method: Regenerate from the published notice identifier.
data_classes.deletion_method: Delete the URL with the local source record.

data_classes.name: buyer_organisation_derived_identifier
data_classes.refresh_method: Recompute from allowlisted official buyer identifiers using the fixed project secret.
data_classes.deletion_method: Delete the derived identifier and dependent records from local storage.

required_gates.reason: The published-notice Search API is officially documented as anonymous and openly accessible to systems and data reusers.
Internal source calibration is within the documented analysis and reuse purposes for published notices.
Published procurement notices may be commercially reused and the API explicitly identifies commercial added-value services as users.
The API is intended for system-based analysis and reuse, while model training and fine-tuning remain outside the intended use.
The allowed notice and metadata classes have no stated maximum retention period and direct contact fields are excluded.
Published notice identifiers, procedure identifiers, and canonical notice locations support reproducible source provenance.
Allowlisted official buyer organisation identifiers can produce stable keyed hashes without retaining contact identities.
All persisted source classes have an explicit local deletion method and direct personal contact fields are outside the contract.
Versioned API documentation, stable identifiers, canonical locations, and refresh paths preserve reproducibility for the allowed fields.

recheck_conditions: Revalidate the TED Search API and legal notice before the recorded deadline.
Re-evaluate feasibility before collecting direct contact fields, attachments, or non-published notices.
Re-evaluate feasibility if model training or fine-tuning enters the intended use.
